independence_scope: intra-mesh Anthropic-family; agreement is corroboration, never cross-provider evidence

reviews.reasoning: Span re-derived against both witnesses. The closing seam web:Ps.42.5|web:Ps.42.6 = oshb:Ps.42.6|oshb:Ps.42.7 is witness-agreed: MT 42:6 ends יְשׁוּע֥וֹת פָּנָֽיו and MT 42:7 opens on the vocative אֱֽלֹהַ֗י, which WEB carries as “My God, my soul is in despair within me.” (web:Ps.42.6), so the address-restart warrant that closes this row is byte-founded and the span itself is right. The refrain claim re-derives exactly: slicing the opening of oshb:Ps.42.6 from source bytes and sweeping the book returns 3 verses at BOTH byte tier and skeleton tier (oshb:Ps.42.6, oshb:Ps.42.12, oshb:Ps.43.5), so the row's 'sweep: 3 verses book-wide, skeleton query' is correct and in fact understates the tier it could have claimed. Title labels match the device inventory for Psalm 42 exactly (maskil, lamnatseach, livnei_qorach), and the shift+1 arithmetic in web:Ps.42.0 = oshb:Ps.42.1 and web:Ps.42.5 = oshb:Ps.42.6 is correct, the title pseudo-ref form being owner-ruled. Two defects, neither touching the span: an out-of-span verse is argued in prose without being mirrored into boundary_evidence_refs (and the mirror checker's GREEN is a false negative produced by this book's own numbering hazard), and the second substrate signal asserts an arithmetic that does not hold for the object it names.

challenges.claim: The row argues web:Ps.42.6 — a verse outside its own span Ps.42.1-Ps.42.5 — in its rationale, but web:Ps.42.6 never appears in boundary_evidence_refs; the refs-mirror rule is satisfied only in appearance, because the token oshb:Ps.42.6 present in the refs is a DIFFERENT verse.
challenges.evidence: The rationale closes 'the address then restarts, ‘My God’ (web:Ps.42.6)'. Psalm 42 is shift+1, so web:Ps.42.6 = oshb:Ps.42.7 (ps_lib.web_to_mt(42,6) returns (42,7)), whereas the refs entry 'web:Ps.42.5 = oshb:Ps.42.6' denotes oshb:Ps.42.6 = web:Ps.42.5, an IN-span verse (ps_lib.mt_to_web(42,6) returns (42,5)). The two are distinct verses sharing the bare token 'Ps.42.6': oshb:Ps.42.6 ends יְשׁוּע֥וֹת פָּנָֽיו while oshb:Ps.42.7 opens אֱֽלֹהַ֗י. Demonstration that the checker is bare-token matched and therefore masked here: check_refs_mirror.py on the row as shipped reports flag_count 0 / GREEN; re-running it on a probe copy identical except that the refs entry 'web:Ps.42.5 = oshb:Ps.42.6' is shortened to 'web:Ps.42.5' reports flag_count 1 with argued_but_unmirrored ['Ps.42.6']. Cure: add web:Ps.42.6 = oshb:Ps.42.7 to boundary_evidence_refs; this is the seam-partner verse of the row's own closing seam, so under the one-edit seam-pair rule it is installed while the neighbouring row's front-seam refs are touched.

challenges.claim: The substrate signal '5 of 11 WEB verses precede the refrain's first return' is arithmetically false for the object it names: 4 WEB verses precede web:Ps.42.5, not 5, and the figure 5 is only correct for a different object (the span's own verse count, which includes the refrain verse rather than preceding it).
challenges.evidence: verse_map_web.json holds 12 keys for Psalm 42: the title pseudo-verse Ps.42.0 plus the numbered verses Ps.42.1 through Ps.42.11, i.e. 11 numbered WEB verses (digit-bearing, unit = WEB verses). The refrain's first return is web:Ps.42.5 = oshb:Ps.42.6 (byte-tier collation of the refrain opening sliced from oshb:Ps.42.6 hits exactly oshb:Ps.42.6, oshb:Ps.42.12, oshb:Ps.43.5 — 3 verses book-wide). The WEB verses preceding web:Ps.42.5 are web:Ps.42.1, web:Ps.42.2, web:Ps.42.3, web:Ps.42.4 = 4 verses, unit = WEB verses. The pair (5, 11) is additionally internally inconsistent: counting the title pseudo-verse Ps.42.0 as a preceding unit does yield 5, but then the denominator is 12 WEB keys, not 11. Cure: either '4 of 11 WEB verses precede the refrain's first return' or '5 of 11 WEB verses run through the refrain's first return', naming the object kept.

reviews.reasoning: The original-language work in this row is unusually careful and I confirm it, including its one NEGATIVE collation claim, which is the kind that normally fails review. The refrain close quoted at oshb:Ps.42.12 collates at byte tier against oshb:Ps.42.12 and against oshb:Ps.43.5, and I further confirm the two verses are byte-identical across their FULL length, not merely at the quoted close; the earlier return's close יְשׁוּע֥וֹת פָּנָֽיו collates at byte tier against oshb:Ps.42.6 and returns tier none against oshb:Ps.42.12, exactly as the row asserts. The shared refrain opening likewise collates at byte tier against all three of oshb:Ps.42.6, oshb:Ps.42.12 and oshb:Ps.43.5, and the book-wide sweep returns 3 verses at byte and skeleton tier alike. The single-YHWH claim re-derives: exactly 1 token יְהוָ֨ה in Psalm 42, at oshb:Ps.42.9 = web:Ps.42.8, matching the device inventory's yhwh 1 for this psalm. The front seam is witness-agreed (oshb:Ps.42.7 opens אֱֽלֹהַ֗י) and the psalm-final close web:Ps.42.11 = oshb:Ps.42.12 is correct shift+1 arithmetic. The rejected_alternative's second sentence carries the mandated rival disclosure, which is the one permitted form. Two defects: the row quotes and cites a ketiv/qere verse with no disclosure, and it ships a divine-name count whose object is never named.

challenges.claim: The row quotes and cites web:Ps.42.8 = oshb:Ps.42.9 as boundary evidence without disclosing that this is one of the book's 65 ketiv/qere verses, a disclosure the campaign requires whenever a K/Q verse is quoted.
challenges.evidence: pmarks_Ps.json kq carries the entry Ps.42.9 with 1 note (the inventory holds 68 notes over 65 verses; Ps.42.9 is the only K/Q verse in Psalms 42, 43 and 44 — the swept membership of those three psalms against the kq inventory returns exactly 1 verse). The row's rationale quotes “Yahweh will command his loving kindness in the daytime” (web:Ps.42.8) and lists web:Ps.42.8 in boundary_evidence_refs; web:Ps.42.8 = oshb:Ps.42.9 under this psalm's shift+1 rule. The K/Q sits in the verse's second colon: the source bytes of oshb:Ps.42.9 carry the unpointed ketiv שירה immediately followed by the pointed qere שִׁיר֣וֹ, and WEB renders the qere at “In the night his song shall be with me” (web:Ps.42.8). Scoped honestly: the K/Q token lies OUTSIDE the colon the row quotes and does not touch the row's YHWH argument, so this is a disclosure defect, not a corrupted warrant — but the disclosure obligation attaches to the verse, and the row both quotes from it and rests boundary evidence on it. Cure: disclose the K/Q (single-witness, WLC) where web:Ps.42.8 is cited.

challenges.claim: The divine-name figures 'Yahweh 1 / Elohim 6 in this psalm' are shipped in the rationale and again in a substrate signal without naming the counted object or unit, and the object is not recoverable by re-derivation: three defensible readings of 'Elohim' yield 3, 6 and 11 for this psalm.
challenges.evidence: The figures themselves match psalm_device_inventory.json yhwh_elohim_per_psalm['42'] = {yhwh: 1, elohim: 6}, so the row is faithful to the inventory; the defect is the unnamed object, which the toolkit expressly requires when these figures are cited. Re-deriving over the source bytes of oshb:Ps.42.1-12, unit = tokens: counting only the bare unsuffixed token, e.g. אֱלֹהִֽים at oshb:Ps.42.2, gives 3 tokens (at MT 42:2, 42:3, 42:5); counting bare plus PREFIXED spellings, e.g. לֵֽ֭אלֹהִים at oshb:Ps.42.6, gives 6 tokens (MT 42:2, 42:3 twice, 42:5, 42:6, 42:12) — this is the inventory's figure; counting every form including suffixed spellings such as אֱֽלֹהַ֗י at oshb:Ps.42.7 gives 11 tokens. A reader re-deriving 'Elohim 6' from the unsuffixed spelling alone lands on 3 and would score the row wrong. Cure: name the object and unit, e.g. 'bare and prefixed spellings, 6 tokens'. Note for the orchestrator: the same ambiguity is a toolkit defect, since TOOLKIT.md describes these figures as token counts of the UNSUFFIXED spellings only, which is not what the inventory actually counts.

reviews.reasoning: The numbering spine of this row is correct where it matters most, and it matters here because Psalm 43 is the only identity-numbered psalm in this cluster. Psalm 43 is absent from the shift+1 membership, so its WEB and MT verses run 1-5 against 1-5 and its own citations require no dual-cite; the row's contrast with its shift+1 neighbour is therefore right. The title-absence claim is factually TRUE on the verse map: Ps.43.0 is not a key in verse_map_web.json, while Ps.38.0, Ps.39.0, Ps.40.0, Ps.41.0 and Ps.42.0 all are. The byte-identity claim is stronger than the row states: oshb:Ps.43.5 and oshb:Ps.42.12 are byte-identical across the FULL verse, and the shared refrain opening sweeps to 3 verses book-wide at byte and skeleton tier alike. The row's handling of the merge rival is correct campaign practice — the 42|43 pairing is a typed cross-psalm relation, so a merge proposal across it is out of scope, and the row names the rival rather than suppressing it, keeping two parents and leaving each psalm's internal movement intact. The bare oshb:Ps.42.12 cite in the substrate signal is the settled author-wave class, not a defect, since the WEB counterpart web:Ps.42.11 is carried in boundary_evidence_refs. One defect, in the evidence field that carries the numbering claim.

challenges.claim: The substrate signal carrying this row's title-absence claim is grammatically objectless and carries no digit-bearing sweep, so the claim a reviewer must audit is not actually stated in it — even though the underlying fact is true.
challenges.evidence: The signal reads 'Psalm 43 has no WEB title pseudo-verse (verified against the WEB verse map, the WEB verse map carries for Psalms 38-42 but not for this psalm)'. The clause 'the WEB verse map carries for Psalms 38-42' has no object — what is carried is never named — and the absence claim ships without the digit-bearing sweep the campaign requires; check_universals.py independently flags this same field (path [2].observed_substrate_signals[0], claim 'has no WEB title pseudo-verse (verified agains'), and flags the parallel wording in the rationale at [2].rationale. Re-derived, the fact is TRUE and countable: of the 5 psalms 38, 39, 40, 41, 42, all 5 carry a WEB title pseudo-verse (Ps.38.0, Ps.39.0, Ps.40.0, Ps.41.0, Ps.42.0 are keys in verse_map_web.json) and Ps.43.0 is not a key; unit = psalms. Psalm 43 also has no entry in psalm_device_inventory.json superscriptions, which holds 116 titled psalms. Cure: restate with the object named and the digit carried, e.g. '5 of 5 psalms 38-42 carry a WEB title pseudo-verse; Psalm 43 carries none'.

reviews.reasoning: The span and its warrant hold. The opening quote collates at byte tier against oshb:Ps.44.2, the shift+1 arithmetic is right at every ref (web:Ps.44.0 = oshb:Ps.44.1, web:Ps.44.1 = oshb:Ps.44.2, web:Ps.44.8 = oshb:Ps.44.9), and the title pseudo-ref form is owner-ruled. The selah handling is exactly what the evidence rules ask for: pmarks_Ps.json holds exactly 1 selah verse in the whole of Psalms 42, 43 and 44, at oshb:Ps.44.9 = web:Ps.44.8, so 'the span's one Selah occurrence (1 verse)' is correct with its unit named, it sits at the row's own close, and the row explicitly demotes it to 'corroborating but not driving the boundary' rather than leaning on it. WEB renders it in-text at “In God we have made our boast all day long. We will give thanks to your name forever. Selah.” (web:Ps.44.8), which is verbatim. The Elohim/YHWH figures match psalm_device_inventory.json for Psalm 44 exactly (elohim 4, yhwh 0) and the row disclaims them as background rather than evidence, so I do not file the count-object point separately here as I do on the row that ships the same figures as evidence. Two observations short of defects: the device note names two of the three title labels the inventory records for Psalm 44 (it omits lamnatseach, which the inventory does carry), which is incomplete but not false; and no device other than the noted selah falls in this span. One defect, in the substrate signal that carries the opening quote.

challenges.claim: The substrate signal labels its quoted Hebrew 'the recollection verb pair', but the bytes it quotes contain one finite verb, not two; the second verb of the pair the label is reaching for lies outside the quoted span, so quote, gloss and label do not cover the same span.
challenges.evidence: The signal quotes the opening of oshb:Ps.44.2 and glosses it 'God, with our ears we have heard'. Within those bytes the only finite verb is שָׁמַ֗עְנוּ; the first two tokens are a vocative and a prepositional phrase. The second recollection verb stands in the NEXT clause of the same verse, which the row does not quote: אֲבוֹתֵ֥ינוּ סִפְּרוּ לָ֑נוּ, rendered by WEB as “our fathers have told us” (web:Ps.44.1). The signal's own continuation, 'naming the fathers' report as the unit's ground', is thus argued from bytes it never puts on the page, and the gloss it does supply carries a single verb, matching the quote and contradicting the label. Since the staged extract has no morphology layer, a part-of-speech label of this kind has to be re-derived from the pointed bytes and both witnesses' renderings, and re-derived that way it fails as stated. Cure under the quote/gloss parity rule: extend the quote through אֲבוֹתֵ֥ינוּ סִפְּרוּ לָ֑נוּ and re-cut the gloss to match, which makes the pair real, or drop 'pair' and keep the present quote.

reviews.reasoning: Nothing in this row fails re-derivation. The opening quote collates at byte tier against oshb:Ps.44.10, and the seam it drives, web:Ps.44.8|web:Ps.44.9 = oshb:Ps.44.9|oshb:Ps.44.10, is witness-agreed: WEB opens the verse “But now you rejected us, and brought us to dishonor” (web:Ps.44.9) against the particle that opens the MT verse, so the adversative turn is carried by both witnesses and the row does not rest it on the English alone. Every dual-cite is correct shift+1 arithmetic (web:Ps.44.9 = oshb:Ps.44.10, web:Ps.44.16 = oshb:Ps.44.17, web:Ps.44.8 = oshb:Ps.44.9). The selah treatment is the model case for the evidence rules: the row locates it on the FRONT seam at web:Ps.44.8 = oshb:Ps.44.9, states plainly that the adversative particle drives the turn 'independently', and leaves selah as corroboration, which is the most it is ever allowed to be. Its span-scoped absence claim, that no additional psalm-level device touches the span, re-derives as TRUE against every inventory: over oshb:Ps.44.10-17 there is no selah (the only selah in Psalms 42-44 is oshb:Ps.44.9), no paseq (the paseq inventory holds Psalm 44 segs at oshb:Ps.44.2, oshb:Ps.44.3, oshb:Ps.44.9 and oshb:Ps.44.24 only, none of them in span), no ketiv/qere (the only K/Q in these three psalms is oshb:Ps.42.9), no inverted nun and no suspended letter (both inventories are empty for Psalms 42-44). The row's glosses of the Hebrew are set in straight quotes rather than the curly quotes reserved for WEB quotation, which is the correct convention and is exactly what one row in this cluster gets wrong. The rejected_alternative is one sentence and names a real rival seam inside the span. No challenge.

The span, the seams and the device claims all hold. The opening quote collates at byte tier against oshb:Ps.44.18, both dual-cites are correct shift+1 arithmetic (web:Ps.44.17 = oshb:Ps.44.18, web:Ps.44.22 = oshb:Ps.44.23), and the verse count re-derives: web:Ps.44.17 through web:Ps.44.22 is 6 verses, unit = WEB verses, as the row states. The device-absence claim is span-scoped and TRUE on every inventory: over oshb:Ps.44.18-23 there is no selah (Psalms 42-44 carry exactly 1, at oshb:Ps.44.9), no paseq (Psalm 44's segs sit at oshb:Ps.44.2, oshb:Ps.44.3, oshb:Ps.44.9, oshb:Ps.44.24), no ketiv/qere, no inverted nun and no suspended letter. The row makes no petuchah or setumah claim in either direction, which is correct for a book whose mark layer is empty by extraction. One defect, and it is the quotation convention rather than the substance: the row dresses a gloss of its own Hebrew in the punctuation the campaign reserves for verbatim WEB, in a field carrying no WEB reference. I note but do not file the rhetorical 'entirely' in the device note, which check_universals flags and which carries no evidentiary weight either way.

challenges.claim: The substrate signal sets a gloss of its quoted Hebrew in curly quotes, the punctuation this campaign reserves for verbatim WEB quotation, in a field that carries no web: reference — and the string so quoted is not verbatim WEB.
challenges.evidence: The signal reads 'the strophe opens on the summarizing demonstrative כָּל זֹ֣את, “all this” (oshb:Ps.44.18), pivoting from accusation to protestation of innocence'. check_web_quotes.py flags this field directly: path [5].observed_substrate_signals[0], quote 'all this', refs_nearby [], issue 'curly quote with NO web: ref in its field' (1 flag over 22 quotes checked in this cluster, the other 21 clean). The string is also not WEB-verbatim: WEB reads “All this has come on us, yet we haven't forgotten you.” (web:Ps.44.17), with an initial capital, so the lower-case form is a gloss of the Hebrew, not a quotation. The row's own rationale handles the same words correctly, curly-quoting the WEB sentence with web:Ps.44.17 inline, and the three sibling rows in this cluster set their Hebrew glosses in straight quotes. Cure: straight-quote the gloss, or curly-quote the WEB string and carry web:Ps.44.17 in the field.

reviews.reasoning: This row's central original-language claim is the one I most expected to fail, and it re-derives exactly. The opening quote collates at byte tier against oshb:Ps.44.24, and the divine-title argument holds on a full-psalm token sweep: across the source bytes of oshb:Ps.44.1-27 the title Adonai occurs exactly 1 time, unit = tokens, in this row's own opening verse oshb:Ps.44.24 = web:Ps.44.23, while every Elohim-bearing token in the psalm (oshb:Ps.44.2, oshb:Ps.44.5, oshb:Ps.44.9, oshb:Ps.44.22, matching the inventory's elohim 4) stands EARLIER and none falls inside oshb:Ps.44.24-27. The row's 'Adonai rather than the Elohim used earlier in the psalm' is therefore byte-true in both directions, and the psalm carries 0 YHWH tokens, so this is not the Psalm 68 rendering zone and no disclosure is owed. WEB carries “Wake up! Why do you sleep, Lord? Arise! Don't reject us forever.” (web:Ps.44.23) verbatim, and both dual-cites are correct shift+1 arithmetic (web:Ps.44.23 = oshb:Ps.44.24, web:Ps.44.26 = oshb:Ps.44.27). The verse count re-derives: web:Ps.44.23 through web:Ps.44.26 is 4 verses, unit = WEB verses. The doxology claim is right — the four book-boundary seams sit at oshb:Ps.41.14, oshb:Ps.72.18-20, oshb:Ps.89.53 and oshb:Ps.106.48, none of them here — so keeping unit_type as strophe rather than coda is correct. The imperative reading cannot be machine-checked, there being no morphology layer, but it is argued from the pointed bytes and corroborated by both witnesses' renderings, which is the prescribed method. I note that oshb:Ps.44.24 carries 2 paseq segs in the inventory; the row asserts no device absence for this span, and paseq is seg-layer material outside the quotable verse bytes, so nothing is owed. No challenge.
